pitch_detail.notes: Sourced anchors: the Yawning Glacier's lower limit is about 6,200 ft and the Magic–Pelton Col is 6,480 ft. Crevassed; rope up. Reached from Pelton Basin by easy slopes and a steep couloir below the glacier toe.
pitch_detail.pitch: Section 1 — Yawning Glacier to the Magic–Pelton Col

pitch_detail.notes: Traverse west across the head of the glacier. The schrund at the base of the rock opens through the season and can be the crux by August. Length apportioned within the sourced col-to-summit interval.
pitch_detail.pitch: Section 2 — from the col, bear back and cross the head of the glacier to the north face

pitch_detail.notes: Sourced: 600 ft of steep rock to a notch immediately northwest of the summit. Broken gneiss, north-facing, often wet or verglassed; slung blocks for anchors, no fixed gear.
From the notch immediately northwest of the summit, a short traverse and easy climb to the top. Length apportioned to close the sourced elevation interval.
